extracted.intended_audience: executive branch agencies, agency heads, regulatory policy officers, OIRA/OMB staff, and agency legal/regulatory staff
extracted.subtask_description: Requirements and procedures for agencies to identify regulatory problems, extend EO 12866 review to guidance documents, notify and consult with OIRA about significant guidance, and to structure agency regulatory plans and approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of specific market failure or problem
rubrics_metrics.description: "Each agency shall identify in writing the specific market failure (such as externalities, market power, lack of information) or other specific problem that it intends to address (including, where applicable, the failures of public institutions) that warrant new agency action, as well as assess the significance of that problem, to enable assessment of whether any new regulation is warranted."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must state in writing the precise market failure or problem motivating any proposed agency action and assess how significant that problem is — examples given include externalities, market power, lack of information, and failures of public institutions. The purpose is to enable assessment of whether new regulation is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend EO 12866 requirements to guidance documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple amendments insert the words "and guidance documents" after "regulations" in sections 1(b)(7), 1(b)(10), 1(b)(11), 1(b)(12), 2(a), 2(b) and elsewhere, indicating EO review obligations apply to guidance documents as well as regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the Executive Order previously referenced only "regulations," agencies are required to apply the same review/consideration language to guidance documents; the order repeatedly amends text to include guidance documents alongside regulations throughout the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Guidance document'
rubrics_metrics.description: "'Guidance document' means an agency statement of general applicability and future effect, other than a regulatory action, that sets forth a policy on a statutory, regulatory, or technical issue or an interpretation of a statutory or regulatory issue."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the operative definition for distinguishing guidance documents from regulatory actions for purposes of applicability of the Order's provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Significant guidance document' — substantive criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: "Significant guidance document' — (1) Means a guidance document disseminated to regulated entities or the general public that, for purposes of this order, may reasonably be anticipated to: (A) Lead to an annual effect of $100 million or more or adversely affect in a material way the economy, a sector of the economy, productivity, competition, jobs, the environment, public health or safety, or State, local, or tribal governments or communities; (B) Create a serious inconsistency or otherwise interfere with an action taken or planned by another agency; (C) Materially alter the budgetary impact of entitlements, grants, user fees, or loan programs or the rights or obligations of recipients thereof; or (D) Raise novel legal or policy issues arising out of legal mandates, the President's priorities, or the principles set forth in this Executive order;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A guidance document meeting any of the listed effects (A–D) when reasonably anticipated is treated as "significant" for purposes of the Order and triggers the special notification/consultation requirements with OIRA. The $100 million threshold is an annual-effect monetary bright-line for one of the tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusions from 'Significant guidance document'
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant guidance document "does not include: (A) Guidance documents on regulations issued in accordance with the formal rulemaking provisions of 5 U.S.C. 556, 557; (B) Guidance documents that pertain to a military or foreign affairs function of the United States, other than procurement regulations and regulations involving the import or export of non-defense articles and services; (C) Guidance documents on regulations that are limited to agency organization, management, or personnel matters; or (D) Any other category of guidance documents exempted by the Administrator of OIRA."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These enumerated categories are carved out from the definition of "significant"; OIRA has discretion to exempt additional categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Policy Office approval before commencing rulemaking or inclusion on the Plan
rubrics_metrics.description: "Unless specifically authorized by the head of the agency, no rulemaking shall commence nor be included on the Plan without the approval of the agency's Regulatory Policy Office, and the Plan shall contain at a minimum: ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency rulemaking initiatives must be approved by the agency's Regulatory Policy Office prior to being commenced or listed on the agency's regulatory plan, unless the agency head provides specific authorization otherwise. This centralizes internal clearance of rulemakings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plan content: anticipated costs/benefits and aggregate estimate
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(c)(1)(B) requires insertion "of each rule as well as the agency's best estimate of the combined aggregate costs and benefits of all its regulations planned for that calendar year to assist with the identification of priorities" after "of the anticipated costs and benefits."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency's Regulatory Plan must include the anticipated costs and benefits for each rule and also an agency-level best estimate of the combined aggregate costs and benefits of all regulations planned for the calendar year to help identify priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Plan content: citation to legal authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 4(c)(1)(C) requires insertion ", and specific citation to such statute, order, or other legal authority" after "court order."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each Plan entry must include a specific citation to the statute, court order, or other legal authority that underlies the rulemaking action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of formal rulemaking for complex determinations in consultation with OIRA
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment: "In consultation with OIRA, each agency may also consider whether to utilize formal rulemaking procedures under 5 U.S.C. 556 and 557 for the resolution of complex determinations" after "comment period of not less than 60 days."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For complex determinations, agencies are directed to consult with OIRA and may consider using formal adjudicative-style rulemaking procedures (5 U.S.C. 556/557) in lieu of standard notice-and-comment where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and notification of a Regulatory Policy Officer (RPO)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Within 60 days of the date of this Executive order, each agency head shall designate one of the agency's Presidential Appointees to be its Regulatory Policy Officer, advise OMB of such designation, and annually update OMB on the status of this designation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must appoint a Presidential Appointee as RPO, notify OMB of the designation promptly, and provide annual updates to OMB regarding that designation. The RPO is charged with ensuring agency compliance with the Order's requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance notification and consultation with OIRA for Significant Guidance Documents
rubrics_metrics.description: New Sec. 9: "Each agency shall provide OIRA, at such times and in the manner specified by the Administrator of OIRA, with advance notification of any significant guidance documents. Each agency shall take such steps as are necessary for its Regulatory Policy Officer to ensure the agency's compliance with the requirements of this section. Upon the request of the Administrator, for each matter identified as, or determined by the Administrator to be, a significant guidance document, the issuing agency shall provide to OIRA the content of the draft guidance document, together with a brief explanation of the need for the guidance document and how it will meet that need. The OIRA Administrator shall notify the agency when additional consultation will be required before the issuance of the significant guidance document."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must notify OIRA in advance about significant guidance, ensure internal RPO oversight, and — upon OIRA request — submit draft content and a brief justification explaining the need and expected effect; OIRA may require additional consultation prior to issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of agency authority
rubrics_metrics.description: "Nothing in this order shall be construed to impair or otherwise affect the authority vested by law in an agency or the head thereof, including the authority of the Attorney General relating to litigation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Order explicitly preserves statutory and other legal authorities of agencies and agency heads (including the Attorney General's litigation-related authority), clarifying that the Order does not supplant or diminish those powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification/removal of 'rule' terminology in definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3 amendments strike references such as "or `rule'" after "`Regulation'" and remove wording like "or rules" in a number of places, and remove phrases like "rule or" from "final rule or regulation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These textual edits reduce the distinction between 'rule' and 'regulation' in the Order's language and harmonize the terminology — part of the broader move to fold guidance documents into the Order's scope.
